anomalies.observed: R3 is a 10 kΩ resistor from +3V3 to /NET0048, which is the gate node of the main-pump low-side MOSFET T1 (IRLR2905, via R52 100 Ω from IO10) and the collector of level-shifter T5. R3 is not on the I2C_SDA or I2C_SCL nets. The main I2C pull-ups are R10 and R24 (2.2 kΩ).
anomalies.expected: The specification describes R3 as a 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-up to +3V3 ("R3/R4 I2C_SDA/I2C_SCL +3V3 2.2k pull-ups"). A pump gate that is pulled up to +3V3 would turn the 24 V main pump on by default whenever T5 is off, so the gate should instead have a pull-down (as the ATO gate does with R46 10 kΩ to GND).
anomalies.impact: Gate of the main circulation-pump MOSFET is pulled toward +3V3 while not actively driven low. The pump may run uncontrolled at power-up or during firmware reset, and the I2C pull-up that the spec describes is not present on the bus.

anomalies.observed: The enable pin (EN, pin 2) of the TPS62933 buck regulator U5 is marked no-connect and is not tied to any net.
anomalies.expected: An enable pin on a buck regulator should be tied to VIN for always-on operation or driven by a defined logic level. A floating EN pin leaves the converter's start-up state undefined.
anomalies.impact: The 5 V rail may fail to start or start unpredictably, which would leave the ESP32 and the 3.3 V LDO without a supply. Whether this is a fault depends on the TPS62933's internal EN pull-up, which the files do not show.

parsed.summary: The netlist is mostly internally consistent, but R3 sits as a 10 kΩ pull-up on the main-pump MOSFET gate, which contradicts the spec's 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-up role and would leave the pump on by default. The buck regulator's unconnected EN pin is a weaker, lower-confidence concern.
